title: POC Weekly: slot-hedge calibration & TTFT tuning
topics: TTFT regression observed during spike window

Agreed on targeted microbench runs and a short rolling canary with adjusted priority queue and KV cache warmup. SE to deliver microburst profiles and AE to share pricing impact for hedging policy.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-08
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (CTO - HavenPay), Elena Park (SRE), Samir Patel (ML Eng)
Shared links: https://redwood.internal/bench/slot-hedge-2027-11 (bench CSV), deck: drive.link/hedge-pilot-deck, prod traces note (dropped)

[00:00] Jordan: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick agenda — priya will run through the microburst numbers we ran overnight, then we talk hedging config and costs, and wrap with next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Marco: yep sounds good, Jordan thanks. apologies — we had a late incident but all stable now.
[00:23] Priya: cool, i'll share my screen in a sec, but summary first: we saw a consistent TTFT bump around the 50-150ms window for streaming sessions when sequence lengths mix above 64, and an extra tail when concurrent streaming sessions hit the burst window. i suspect a cache-warmup plus kernel fallback interaction.
[00:45] Samir: when you say kernel fallback, do you mean the runtime is switching to slower GEMM kernel at runtime? we've seen that with some of the quant profiles yes.
[00:53] Priya: yeah exactly — so on the bench we flagged two kernel paths: path A (fast for seqlen <=64) and path B (better memory layout for >=128) — during microbursts the router sometimes chooses B after a few tokens which makes the TTFT jump. also KV cache cold-start matters for streaming, prefix not hitting cache.
[01:15] Elena: is KV spelled out in the logs as K V cache or something else? our ingestion sometimes munges that field and can't correlate.
[01:22] Priya: annoyingly the transcription / logs sometimes call it KV-cache, K-V cache, or kvcacher so correlating is annoying. we'll include the exact tracer tags in the runbook.
[01:30] Jordan: priya do you have numbers? like 50th, 95th, 99th for TTFT split by seqlen buckets?
[01:36] Priya: yes — i put them in the bench CSV. quick highlights: seqlen <=32 median TTFT 60ms, 95th 95ms; seqlen 64 median 75ms, 95th 140ms; seqlen 128 median 110ms, 95th 320ms with a long tail to 700ms in the spike test. for streaming microburst test (100 concurrent short streams) the 99th shot up to ~900ms in worst-case.
[02:10] Marco: ouch. is that reproduced on Dedicated or only on Hosted? this is our dedicated pool on the pilot, right?
[02:17] Samir: yes pilot is running in Redwood Dedicate — i meant Dedicated — the pilot nodes are the reserved gpus. we've got dedicated pool but still hitting this.
[02:25] Jordan: common question — differences between dedicated and hosted runtime shouldn't cause kernel selection differences except if compilation flags differ. priya, did you check kernel flags?
[02:33] Priya: i ran two profiles: flags set A (aggressive fused attention) vs flags set B (compat/legacy GEMM). the dedicated AMI we used was missing the newer kernel 2.1 build so fallback happened. we can reproduce locally by toggling the env var.
[02:49] Elena: is upgrading kernels part of the pilot? do we have permission?
[02:53] Jordan: yes we can push kernel upgrades in the pilot window — but that needs a short maintenance window and Marco's sign-off.
[02:59] Marco: i'm ok but want the rollback plan.
[03:03] Jordan: rollback is quick — revert AMI and switch kernel flag off, will take <15 minutes and we keep a snapshot. we'll include exact runbook.
[03:12] Priya: separately we tested slot-hedge: enable a 15% slot reserve for streaming priority and route long-seqlen to a 'warm' lane that keeps KV warm. it reduced 95th by ~35% in synthetic, but increased avg cost by ~7% due to reserved idle slots.
[03:34] Samir: can you run the same with seqlen distribution matching our production traces? i think our mix is heavier on 64-128.
[03:41] Priya: yes that is itemized in action items — i will run seq buckets 16/32/64/128/256 with the two kernel flags and both with/without slot-hedge.
[03:52] Marco: what's the impact on throughput? if we reserve slots won't we throttle other workloads?
[03:58] Priya: tradeoff — slot-hedge pins capacity for streaming, we saw a small backlog increase for batch endpoints but throughput was stable because the router prefers batch lanes for non-streaming workloads. still, need to tune autoscaler to allow burst capacity for mixed traffic.
[04:17] Elena: does Redwood Optimize suggest autoscaler changes or is that manual?
[04:22] Jordan: Redwood Optimize can recommend batch sizes and QPS thresholds; for core autoscale we typically set a mixed policy: base reserved for 70% sustained, spike margin for 30% burst. we'll propose numbers in the pricing note.
[04:36] Samir: question about streaming handshake — can we prepend a short prefix to warm the KV and avoid the cold miss? like a 2-token warm ping?
[04:45] Priya: yep warming prefix helps; the downside is it adds tokens and cost for every stream. we tested micro-warm prefix of 3 tokens and it shaved 95th by ~60ms at cost +0.4% tokens. for high-volume streams cost adds up.
[05:03] Jordan: we'll quantify cost per million streams in the pricing delta. Samir, would that be an acceptable trade if cost delta is small?
[05:12] Samir: possibly, depends on SLA.
[05:15] Marco: on security notes, we'll need SAML/SSO proof for pilot operators and audit logs for KV access. we raised that with legal.
[05:24] Jordan: yes we have SOC2 docs and the audit-log export samples; i'll share the security pack after the call.
[05:30] Elena: also encryption K M S key rotation — we need to confirm KMS integration for the Dedicated pool.
[05:37] Priya: noted — i'll add KMS checklist to the runbook.
[05:42] Jordan: ok priya can you walk quickly through the microbench chart you uploaded?
[05:46] Priya: sure, i'm looking at the CSV now — synthetic microburst test: configured 100 concurrent streams for 30s, seq mix heavy on 64 and 128, kernel flag A vs B. on flag A with slot-hedge: median 68ms, 95th 110ms, 99th 240ms. without slot-hedge on same flag: median 72ms, 95th 165ms, 99th 480ms. flag B overall slower median but less variance.
[06:20] Samir: so heuristic: prefer flag A for normal, but if we see variance > X we fall back to B? can we automate that?
[06:28] Priya: automating kernel hedging is on our roadmap; currently router policies support per-request hints so you can route by predicted sequence length, but dynamic kernel swap mid-request is risky. better to route to a lane compiled with the correct kernel.
[06:44] Marco: how do we detect predicted seq len? our clients don't always pass expected length.
[06:50] Priya: you can pass a hint header with expected_length, or Redwood can infer from prompt length distribution. we discussed adding a quick classifier at the edge to tag long requests.
[06:59] Jordan: Samir, can your client library add an optional header?
[07:03] Samir: yes, we can add expected_length header — backwards compatible.
[07:06] Jordan: great, that'll help routing.
[07:09] Elena: question about fallback policy — if a request times out on the fast lane does it retry on the warm lane? what's the retry policy?
[07:16] Priya: default is a single retry with exponential backoff and fallback to compatible model variant; for streaming we prefer not to retry mid-stream. we can set immediate fallback for short requests to avoid dead time.
[07:28] Marco: okay i want to avoid double-charging customers for retries — make sure billing is clear in the pricing note.
[07:34] Jordan: yes noted — we'll show example billing scenarios.
[07:38] Priya: another note — we saw a small memory cliff on one node when we pushed quantized weights and the kernel B tried to allocate a slightly different buffer. patch is in staging; if customer wants we can pin quantization profile.
[07:53] Samir: can you log that as a recommended quant profile? we prefer to avoid runtime allocation surprises.
[07:58] Priya: absolutely, will include recommended quantization per model.
[08:01] Jordan: okay time check — we've got about 40 minutes left so plenty.
[08:05] Marco: quick ask — could you run a short canary with slot-hedge at 10% for 24 hours and we can measure real-prod impact?
[08:13] Priya: yes, but we need traces and permission; also autoscaler trial to allow a small burst headroom.
[08:18] Marco: i'll sign off if the runbook shows rollback.
[08:21] Jordan: perfect, we'll assemble the runbook.
[08:24] Priya: timeline i'll propose: microbench runs finish by 11/12, SE writeup same day; Jordan shares pricing delta 11/10; if all good we start canary 11/16 for 24-48 hours.
[08:37] Samir: for microbench please also include a run with a 3-token warm prefix.
[08:41] Priya: added.
[08:43] Elena: also confirm Grafana spans — i'll enable early handshake trace and share link.
[08:48] Jordan: great. any other blockers?
[08:51] Marco: none from me. just please include the rollback and estimated cost.
[08:56] Jordan: noted. last question — competitors, have you looked at Anthropic's flow for streaming? they do something similar with a handshake ping to warm models.
[09:04] Marco: we've benchmarked them on latency but not at this scale.
[09:08] Jordan: ok we can share a short doc comparing approaches but the core decision is whether slot-hedge + warm prefix is acceptable given the cost.
[09:16] Priya: i'll draft an ops playbook and bench summary.
[09:20] Jordan: cool — to recap next steps: priya microbench + writeup, jordan pricing and security pack, customer provide traces and enable spans, follow-up meeting next Monday 11/15. action items in the doc. thanks everyone.
[09:34] Marco: thanks all.
[09:36] End of recording.
